chapters.name: History of Nepal
chapters.introduction: Covers ancient, medieval, and modern Nepal including unification, Shah dynasty, Rana regime, democracy, and recent political changes.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-20 marks. History of Nepal and democracy-related questions appear every year.

topics.name: Unification of Nepal
topics.explanation: Prithvi Narayan Shah unified Nepal from small principalities (1743-1775). Key battles: Nuwakot (1744), Kirtipur, Kathmandu Valley (1768-1769). He is known as the Father of Nepal.
keyPoints: Prithvi Narayan Shah = Father of Nepal
'Asali Hindustan' – Nepal as true Hindu kingdom
topics.examTip: Memorise key dates: 1743 (P.N. Shah born), 1768 (Kathmandu captured), 1775 (P.N. Shah died).

topics.name: Democracy and Constitution
topics.explanation: Nepal's political journey: 1951 (end of Rana regime), 1959 (first election), 1960 (party ban), 1990 (multiparty democracy), 2006 (People's Movement II), 2008 (Republic), 2015 (new Constitution).
keyPoints: 3 levels of government: federal, provincial, local
topics.examTip: Know the 7 provinces and their capitals for map questions.

chapters.name: Physical Geography of Nepal
chapters.introduction: Nepal's physical features: Himalayan, Hilly, and Terai zones. Rivers, climate, population distribution, and natural resources.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-18 marks. Map-based and descriptive geography are standard SEE questions.

topics.name: Physiographic Regions
topics.explanation: Nepal has three physiographic regions: (1) Himalayan region (>3000m, sparsely populated), (2) Hilly region (Middle mountains, most populated), (3) Terai (flat plain, highly fertile, southern Nepal). Each has distinct climate, vegetation, and economy.
topics.examTip: Label all three zones and major mountains/rivers on a map for full map marks.

topics.name: Rivers and Climate
topics.explanation: Nepal has three river systems: Koshi (east), Gandaki (central), Karnali (west). Climate varies by region — tropical Terai, temperate hills, cold Himalayas. Monsoon brings 80% of annual rainfall.
topics.examTip: Draw the map of Nepal showing major rivers and their directions.

chapters.name: Constitution, Rights and Democracy
chapters.introduction: Fundamental rights and duties, Constitution of Nepal 2072, structure of government, electoral system, and democracy.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-18 marks. Fundamental rights are guaranteed questions in SEE.

topics.name: Fundamental Rights and Duties
topics.explanation: Constitution of Nepal 2072 guarantees: Right to equality, freedom, justice, education, health, employment, social security, property, religion, and constitutional remedies. Duties include: paying taxes, compulsory education, obeying law.
keyPoints: Right to Education: free and compulsory up to basic level
Duties: pay taxes, vote, environmental protection
topics.examTip: List rights with their article numbers for detailed answers.

chapters.name: Economic Development
chapters.introduction: Basics of Nepal's economy, resources, development indicators, poverty, employment, and agriculture's role.
chapters.whyItMatters: 10-12 marks. Development indicators and economic activities are common short-answer questions.

topics.name: Resources and Development
topics.explanation: Nepal's resources: agricultural land, forests, water, minerals, tourism. Agriculture employs ~60% of workforce. GDP growth depends on remittances, tourism, and hydroelectricity. Poverty line, HDI, and Human Development Index are key development measures.
keyPoints: Nepal is a federal democratic republic
topics.examTip: Know the current five-year plan objectives and budget priorities briefly.
